$ FIXTURE_UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 go test ./b  # pkg-b-echo
--- PASS: TestCorpus
    --- PASS: TestCorpus/script
        --- PASS: TestCorpus/script/twice
            --- PASS: TestCorpus/script/twice/echo
PASS
$ go test  # pkg-a
    the column echo is owned by . and ./b, each as a suite. Column names are unique per corpus root, and one package owns each column.
        Rename one of the suites, or remove one.
    testdata/script/twice.txtar: no registry claims out/shout/outcome and out/shout/values.txt: no column named shout runs over the corpus script.
        If a column should write them, register the column. If not, run hypercase strip -root . -column shout at the module root, then FIXTURE_UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 go test ./... until it changes nothing. The strip removes shout's sections from every archive under the module-root corpus, and the update writes back each one a registry claims, but not one whose cell the update writes nothing for, such as a cell that faults.
    script/twice: A1 is twice B1. The root package, ., prints it with echo, and ./b with shout.
        echo: Does what the case's do/ tree says.
        out/echo/values.txt differs (-golden +got):
        - A1 SIX
        + A1 6
        If the change is intended, run FIXTURE_UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 go test ./... and read the diff before committing.
--- FAIL: TestCorpus
    --- FAIL: TestCorpus/script
        --- FAIL: TestCorpus/script/twice
            --- FAIL: TestCorpus/script/twice/echo
FAIL
[exit 1]
